Dr. Penny Clifton
Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery
Central Hospital
Main Street
Stillwater
22.08.2015
Dear Dr. Clifton
Re: Mrs. Mary Clarke
, DOB 17.09.1960
I am pleased to refer Mrs. Clarke whose signs and symptoms are suggestive of bronchogenic carcinoma to you for further assessment and investigations as you think appropriate.
Mrs. Clarke is a 54-year-old office clerk who smokes cigarettes for more than 30 years. She doesn’t take any medication and has no known allergies. She has a positive family history of laryngeal carcinoma and lung disease. 
Initially, on 04.07.2015 she was presented complaining of a 7-week history of dry non-productive cough which commenced with flu-like symptoms. Augmentin was prescribed and as a result, cough was treated.
On today’s visit, she is complaining of a mild shortness of breath especially at night and heaviness in chest. 
On examination, her pulse was 80 bpm and her temperature 36.7 c. Respiratory examination showed signs of consolidation associated with monophasic wheeze in right mid-zone. Other systemic examinations were normal. Her sputum cytology was normal, too. Chest X-ray and CT revealed right middle lobe atelectasis and enlarged right hilum. 
I would be grateful if you take over her further investigations and assessment as you think appropriate. 
Please don’t hesitate to contact me if you require any further information. 
Yours faithfully
Dr. Reza
